title: Tiered Warmup and Unpin Playbook (personal notes)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a personal scratchpad for a tiered warmup -> unpin -> monitor flow I want to try on medium-risk model flips (non-breaking compat changes, tokenizer tweaks, small perf deltas). Focus is on momentum-based unpinning (increase client fraction when signals look healthy), explicit gravity cohorts (anchor groups that stay pinned longer), and fast off-ramps if regressions appear.

High level idea (one-liner):
- Start with very small live cohorts, warm caches and kv-state, then progressively raise unpinned fraction in staged increments keyed to telemetry signals rather than fixed timers. Use anchor cohorts to stabilize heavy clients and a momentum thermostat to prevent oscillation.

Questions I'm still unsure about:
- How sensitive should thresholds be to noisy latency spikes from infra flakiness vs model regressions?
- Best way to choose "anchor" clients — top spenders, longest sessions, or random sample?
- Should warmup include synthetic primer requests to fill KV cache for long-tail prompts, or leave warming strictly traffic-driven?

Quick glossary (my terms):
- anchor cohort: clients pinned to stable version for longer to act as baseline and reduce churn.
- gravity cohort: small set of clients that hold state that new model must not destabilize (e.g., long chat threads).
- momentum unpin: raise exposure fraction only if a lookback window shows stable growth in success metrics.
- thermostat: dampening factor that reduces next-step unpin if any signal degraded.

Preflight checklist (before any warmup/unpin):
- Confirm rollout PR merged and image pinned: release-manager PR and terraform changes verified.
- Smoke test on staging routing: run canonical prompts (see linked_artifacts) and check tokens, output shape, and basic safety filters.
- Capacity sanity: ensure autoscaler headroom >= 30% under expected ramp.
- Canary alerting: create a temporary alert channel and a short-lived dashboard with these metrics — p50/p90/p99 latency, error-rate (server and application), cost-per-1000 tokens, and quality failure rate (from eval set).
- Notify CS/partners for customers known to be sensitive.

Warmup phase (0 -> 2%):
- Timebox: 20–40 minutes depending on cache warm needs.
- Steering: pick 0.5% traffic from low-risk clients (random small users) + 1.5% synthetic internal clients that exercise long-tail prompts.
- Actions: run 5 canonical prompts per replication key to prime KV. Watch KV-hit-rate, tail latency, and transient OOM logs.
- Stop condition: sustained errors > 0.3% or p99 latency > baseline + 50ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows -> abort and rollback.

Momentum unpin schedule (example):
- Stage A: 2% -> 10% after 30-60m if all signals green.
- Stage B: 10% -> 30% after 60-120m with stricter lookback (longer windows).
- Stage C: 30% -> 60% if stable for 3 hours.
- Stage D: 60% -> 100% after 12 hours and manual sign-off if any VIPs noted.

Each step requires:
- 0.5% absolute improvement margin (or stability) in error-rate and quality pass-rate over previous window OR
- No more than 5% relative regression in token-cost and <10% relative regression in p99 latency.

Anchor cohorts
- Keep 5–10% of top spenders always pinned for 24–48h. Rationale: reduces blast radius on expensive client workloads and provides an immediate baseline to compare quality regressions.
- Rotate anchors weekly to avoid stale biases.

Signals and dashboards (my minimum):
- System: p50/p90/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queued requests, instance churn, OOM events.
- Surface errors: 500s, 429s, model runtime exceptions, decode errors.
- Quality: automated eval pass-rate on a short canned prompt set, top-20 client rejection/quality flags, human review sample (10 messages per stage).
- Cost: tokens-in, tokens-out, approximate cost per 1k tokens.
- Usage morphology: average sequence length, median KV-hit-rate, batch sizes.

Safety ladder (fast off-ramps):
- Level 1 (soft): auto-scale down unpinned fraction by 50% if any single metric crosses threshold for 5m.
- Level 2 (moderate): full immediate rollback to previous image if: error-rate doubles on p90 or quality pass-rate drops by >6% in 30m.
- Level 3 (hard): emergency route to maintenance if catastrophic 5xx storm or data leak detection.

Manual interventions and playbook commands (notes to self):
- rollback command: runbook link + quick CLI: release-manager rollback --to-tag <previous> --drain-cohort anchors-first
- pin client: curl admin endpoint to pin specific client id to old image (used for VIP customers)
- force-warm: run the warmup synthetic script to prefill caches for a cohort (scripting in repo: tools/warmers/fill_kv.py)

Observability & experiment hygiene:
- Keep short-lived dashboards per rollout with annotated stage start/stop.
- Snapshot logs at stage boundaries and upload to cloud storage: logs/rollouts/<date>-<tag>.tar.gz.
- Store a prompt-to-response diff sample for each stage for audit.
- Keep a human-review ballot winner/loser tag on whether behavioral deltas are acceptable.

Post-rollback postmortem anchors (if we roll back):
- Capture: earliest detection metric, detection method, who triaged, sequence of actions, time-to-rollback.
- Root cause hypothesis: infra vs model.
- Recovery checklist: follow-up deploy with additional instrumentation; add more synthetic warmup tests.

Short TODOs (me):
- Draft a tiny CLI to automate momentum heuristics and schedule (prototype: ~1 day).
- Add an automated KV warmup runner to release-manager repo.
- Convince SREs to allow synthetic warmup traffic in low-traffic windows.
- Run a smoke run on canary image 2024-11-15 and iterate thresholds.

Notes to self:
- Keep the language simple when explaining to PMs: "we're raising exposure when signals are consistently healthy, not on a timer".
- Make anchor cohorts visible on billing dash so finance understands risk tradeoffs.
- When in doubt, slow down. Momentum is seductive; cooling periods reduce oscillation and noisy rollouts.

Unresolved experiments (ideas):
- Use Bayesian bandit to select next-step fraction (rather than fixed increments) — could reduce wasted exposure but adds complexity.
- Weight anchors by session-length deciles instead of top-spenders. This might better reflect long-lived stateful workloads.
- Compare pure traffic-driven warmup vs synthetic primer for KV hits on long-tail prompts.

References and quick links:
- Release-manager PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-manager/pull/428
- Slack thread: #releases Nov-01-2024 (linked_artifacts)
- Playbook snippets: tools/warmers/README.md

End of notes. This doc is messy on purpose — it's my living checklist. Will refine into a PR-runbook if we like outcomes from the next trial.
